subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Password Managers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Password Managers usable.

hook.text: The average person has over 100 online accounts. Nobody can remember 100 unique, strong passwords.

buildup.text: Password managers generate and store unique passwords for every site, locked behind one master password.

discovery.text: They encrypt your password vault locally. Even the manager company can't see your stored passwords.

twist.text: If the password manager itself gets breached — like LastPass in 2022 — all your eggs are in one basket.

climax.text: Password managers are imperfect but far safer than reusing 'password123' across a hundred websites.

punchline.text: One strong password protects a hundred others.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of using a password manager?
options: If the manager is breached, all stored passwords could be exposed
They only work on desktop computers
